Two near-identical helpers run work on a single-threaded apartment: `in_sta` in crates/folio-app/src/dialogs.rs and `in_apartment` in folio-core's win::recycle. Keep one, in folio-core's win module, and use it from both without changing behaviour: the CI fix's rule (docs/specs/windows-adapter.md §4: hold the process MTA so a teardown never unloads a cached WinRT factory) and the Recycle Bin's COM threading stay as they are. The commit "fix(app): keep COM initialized so cached WinRT factories stay valid" explains the rule. Tests for both callers. After landing, the CI run on main (Windows Server 2022, where the crash showed) must stay green.

Goal: when the intent of an in-app move that a crash interrupted can no longer be reconciled (its files, folders or metadata changed, or the catalog was recreated), library_status says so with an unavailable reason of its own instead of catalogFailed, and a confirmed command discards the move. Discarding never moves or deletes the user's files and never overwrites an authored metadata file that no longer matches the journal's images; it removes the journal, and a full scan rebuilds the catalog from the disk and the authored metadata. Write the contract into ipc-m1 (§6 and §20), regenerate the bindings and, in the same lane, update the fake shell in apps/desktop/src/ipc/mock/ and its fingerprint (roadmap §4 rule 2). rules: 先合并，再开新 lane：review 完的 lane 尽快 land
合约先行：合约 lane 先 land，核心和界面再并行；重新生成 bindings 时同一个 lane 更新假 shell 和指纹
stack 只给真实依赖，最多两层
按目录分所有权：核心 crates/folio-core/src/<模块>/**，界面 apps/desktop/src/<视图>/**
拆开热点文件：命令按功能组、文案按视图、registry 只改一行、依赖由 chore/build-deps-* 集中装
并行上限：Rust session 最多 3 个，界面最多 4 个，另加 Cowork；pnpm e2e 用 app lock 排队
独占操作放在同步点：but land、but pull、装依赖
每个 lane 同样收尾：pnpm check + pnpm e2e → /code-review（+ /security-review）→ /simplify → 中文汇报 → 你批准 → but land（Codex lane 见下一条）
Codex lane（标着 Codex 的后端 lane）：用「交给 Codex」提示词开工，Codex 自己跑完检查、code-review 和 simplify 后停在 review；再开 Claude Code session 用「Claude 快速审计」提示词：一次 /code-review，涉及特权层再加 /security-review，不重跑 /simplify
路线图数据随 lane 更新：开工、到 review、合并前各跑一次 pnpm roadmap status，只改自己那一条

land: Folio: land {lane} (docs/roadmap/roadmap.json, landing queue). I approve landing it once the checks are green.
1. Read CLAUDE.md §7, every file in .agents/lanes/ and .agents/lanes/{laneFile}.md; run `but status` and `but pull --check`.
2. Confirm from the lane file that /code-review, /security-review where it applies, and /simplify are done; if one is missing, run it and fix findings with commits on the branch.
3. Take the app lock (CLAUDE.md §7.5), run `pnpm check` and `pnpm e2e`, release the lock.
4. Mark it done in the roadmap (`pnpm roadmap status {lane} done`) and commit that one entry on {lane}.

5. Land one lane at a time: check that no other lane is landing and that the previous land's CI run on main has finished green (a land is workspace-wide, CLAUDE.md §7.4: run it only when every other active lane is at checkpoint, review or done, or after telling me), then `but land {lane} --yes`, `but status`, delete the lane file and check the CI run on main. Stop at the first conflict or failure and report it; never use --ai.
reviewCodex: Folio: review and land the Codex lane {lane} (docs/roadmap/roadmap.json). I approve landing it once your reviews pass and the checks are green.

1. Read CLAUDE.md, every file in .agents/lanes/, .agents/lanes/{laneFile}.md and the review scope in ../folio-agent-work/tasks/{taskDir}/claude-review-handoff.md. Run `but status` and `but pull --check`.

2. Set the roadmap entry to wip (`pnpm roadmap status {lane} wip --next "Claude Code review"`). Take over the lane for review: /code-review (high effort for a large lane), /security-review and /simplify on its commits, following the handoff's focus list. Fix findings with commits on the branch; stop and ask me if a finding needs a product or security decision.
3. Take the app lock (CLAUDE.md §7.5), run `pnpm check` and `pnpm e2e`, release the lock.

4. If the lane has not, add its progress line to the ADR and spec items it finishes (for commands: ADR-0004 action item 3 and docs/specs/ipc-m1.md §21). Mark it done (`pnpm roadmap status {lane} done`) and commit that entry on the branch.

5. Land one lane at a time: check that no other lane is landing and that the previous land's CI run on main has finished green (a land is workspace-wide, CLAUDE.md §7.4: run it only when every other active lane is at checkpoint, review or done, or after telling me), then `but land {lane} --yes`, `but status`, delete the lane file and check the CI run on main. Stop at the first conflict or failure and report it; never use --ai.
landRoadmap: Folio: land the stack docs/docs-roadmap-board → docs/docs-roadmap-explorer → chore/build-commit-identity (docs/roadmap/README.md). Docs and tooling only. I approve landing it once the checks are green.
1. Read CLAUDE.md §7, every file in .agents/lanes/ and the three lane files; run `but status` and `but pull --check`.
2. Run `pnpm roadmap doctor` and mark every lane that has landed since the data was written as done (`pnpm roadmap status <lane> done`); commit that on docs/docs-roadmap-explorer.
3. Run `pnpm check` (it starts with the commit and roadmap checks); docs and scripts need no e2e.

4. `but land chore/build-commit-identity --whole-stack --yes`, `but status`, delete the three lane files and check both workflow runs on main (CI and Commits). Stop at the first conflict or failure; never use --ai.
5. Republish the explorer (docs/roadmap/README.md, Publish) so its link shows main's data.
start: Folio lane {lane} (docs/roadmap/roadmap.json: {milestone}, {phase}). Goal, from the roadmap: {summary}

Read CLAUDE.md, every file in .agents/lanes/ and the lane's entry (`pnpm roadmap show {lane}`: what it depends on, what it unblocks, its links). Write the lane file and set the entry to wip (`pnpm roadmap status {lane} wip`).
Follow the feature pipeline in CLAUDE.md §4.2 for this kind of lane (engineering:system-design first for backend or IPC work; a handoff spec first for UI).

Finish with `pnpm check` and `pnpm e2e` under the app lock (CLAUDE.md §7.5), /code-review, /security-review if it touches the privileged layer or IPC, and /simplify; set the entry to review and report to me in Chinese.
codexHandoff: Folio Codex lane {lane}: {title} ({milestone}, {phase}). Backend Rust only. Work in D:/CS Projects Repositories/Files & Backup/Folio (REPO); scratch and review notes go in D:/CS Projects Repositories/Files & Backup/folio-agent-work/tasks/{taskDir}/ (WORK).
Read REPO/AGENTS.md and REPO/CLAUDE.md in full first: on policy they win over this prompt. Reply to me in Simplified Chinese; code, tests, commits, specs and lane records in English.
Depends on: {deps} (all landed on main unless the roadmap says to stack on one).
Shared files, small additive hunks only: {shared}.
Read before coding: {links}; the accepted ADRs and docs/specs/ipc-m1.md for any command or event.

1. `but status` and `but pull --check`; read every file in REPO/.agents/lanes/ and `pnpm roadmap show {lane}`. Start only when fewer than three sessions write Rust and no active lane owns a path you need; otherwise stop and tell me.

2. Write REPO/.agents/lanes/{laneFile}.md (CLAUDE.md §7.3), create the branch with `but branch new {lane}` (`--above <lane>` only for an unlanded dependency) and run `pnpm roadmap status {lane} wip --next "Codex: implementing"`.

3. system-design against the specs and ADRs before coding. A missing contract or a costly decision: stop and ask me. Never change the IPC contract (generated bindings, the fake shell) unless this lane owns it; never hand-edit apps/desktop/src/ipc/bindings.ts.

4. Implement with tests in the same commits: failure, crash-recovery and migration cases where they apply, disposable data only. Commit only your own files or hunks: `but commit -b {lane} -m "<type>(<scope>): <summary>" <ids>`. Commits are Sirui's: no Codex, model, session or co-author lines; never `--ai`.

5. Finish: `pnpm check`, then `pnpm e2e` under the app lock (CLAUDE.md §7.5; remove the lock only if you took it). Run code-review, ponytail (simplify), and the security skills (differential-review, unsafe-checker) when the lane touches the privileged layer, IPC, capabilities or unsafe/FFI code; fix what they find. Record results with `pnpm roadmap gate {lane} check=pass e2e=pass codeReview=pass simplify=pass` (securityReview too when it applies).

6. Write WORK/claude-review-handoff.md for a short Claude Code audit: commits, behaviour, exact check results, the three to five places most worth a second look, open risks and any frontend handoff (command, types, errors). Then `pnpm roadmap status {lane} review --next "Claude audit"`, commit that entry on the branch and stop: no push, no land.
Report to me in Chinese: branch, what changed, exact check results, risks and anything the frontend needs.
codexAudit: Folio: quick Claude Code audit of the Codex lane {lane}: {title}. Run at {auditModel} · {auditEffort}. Codex is trusted: check its work, do not redo it. I approve landing it once the audit passes and the checks are green.
1. Read CLAUDE.md §7, .agents/lanes/{laneFile}.md and ../folio-agent-work/tasks/{taskDir}/claude-review-handoff.md; run `but status` and `but pull --check`.

2. One /code-review pass over the lane's commits, aimed at the handoff's hot spots: correctness, swallowed errors, new or changed types, data safety. Add /security-review only if the lane touches the privileged layer, IPC, capabilities or unsafe code. Codex's own simplify pass counts; skip /simplify.
3. Fix small findings with a commit on {lane}. A finding that needs a redesign, or a product or security decision: stop and report it to me; it goes back to Codex.
4. Take the app lock (CLAUDE.md §7.5), run `pnpm check` and `pnpm e2e`, release the lock. Record the gates, mark the lane done (`pnpm roadmap status {lane} done`) and commit that entry on the branch.

5. Land one lane at a time, after the previous land's main CI has finished: `but land {lane} --yes`, `but status`, delete the lane file, check the CI run on main. Stop at the first conflict or failure; never use --ai.
Report to me in Chinese: findings, fixes and check results.
